correctness.rationale: The prime-power identities give multiplicativity. Squarefree-ratio injectivity is proved by canceling a common squarefree gcd, using the largest prime \(p\ge5\) to exclude a divisor of the corresponding divisor sum, and directly checking \(\{2,3\}\). Every \(n\) has a unique pairwise-coprime powerful/squarefree/rough decomposition. Fixed powerful and rough parts admit at most one squarefree factor per target value. Fan–Pomerance Theorem 1 supplies \(\Phi(X,y)<(3/5)X/\log y\). The powerful reciprocal sum equals \(\zeta(2)\zeta(3)/\zeta(6)\) and its tail is \(O(z^{-1/2})\), via the unique \(a^2b^3\) representation. The resulting bound is \(3A x/[5(1/2-\varepsilon)\log x]+O(x^{1-\varepsilon})\); taking the limsup first, then \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), gives \((6/5)A\). The finite computation is explicitly not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Trudgian asks whether equality occurs infinitely often and lists examples; OEIS supplies more examples. The complete published sign-density result concerns strict inequality, and the exponent classification covers only \(p^a q\) for \(2\le a\le49\). The Erdős–Wintner continuous limiting distribution gives qualitative zero density, not this quantified prime-scale rate. Fan–Pomerance proves the needed general rough-number sieve theorem, but not the derived divisor-sum level-set theorem. No equivalent or dominating count was identified in targeted searches; this does not certify uniqueness.

value.rationale: The motivating 2013 paper explicitly asks whether the arithmetic-function equality occurs infinitely often. An unconditional count \(O(x/\log x)\) for its entire unrestricted solution set, uniformly across every positive target ratio, is a quantitative structural restriction far stronger than finite examples or an unquantified zero-density observation. It applies to integers with arbitrarily many prime factors through the natural squarefree/powerful/rough decomposition and an independently proved sieve ingredient. Optimality and infinitude are not claimed.
